title: Likelihood-based calibration improves the clinical utility of JAG1 functional data for variant classification.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the MaveDB score set urn:mavedb:00001198-a-1 (JAG1 membrane expression, CC0 licence, 735 KB CSV): 2,832 rows, 17 columns; continuous 'score' (0 to 1.17) with std/CI and 7 replicate columns (replicate pairwise correlation 0.45-0.76, under 2% missing per replicate); truth_set has 69 pathogenic + 106 benign; functional_consequence normal 2,346 / likely_abnormal 209 / abnormal 277; 638 synonymous rows, 0 nonsense, 2,288 unique protein changes. MaveDB metadata gives the target as JAG1 exons 1-7 with the DNA sequence included. GitHub repo tris-10/JAG1-Variant-Reclassification holds only one R script (KDE-based LLRp, a log-likelihood ratio of pathogenicity) plus README; no data file.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The new LLRp evidence bins (strong 1, moderate 340, supporting 269) and the 29-VUS (variant of uncertain significance) clinical cohort are in Table S1/S2 and the MaveDB calibration record, which I did not download (Europe PMC supplement endpoint timed out). That 2,194 rows are missense comes from the 2024 source paper as reported in search results; I did not recount it.

a1_downloadable.note: MaveDB REST API returned the full CSV without login; CC0 licence. Verified.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The measured membrane-localization score is the 'score' column; clinical truth labels are in 'truth_set'. Nothing to construct. Verified in file.

a3_inputs_present.note: HGVS (standard variant notation) nucleotide and protein changes plus the full target DNA sequence in MaveDB metadata; mutant sequences derivable in one script. Verified.

a4_units_stated.note: Score is a dimensionless sorting-based ratio on a single 0 to ~1.2 scale from one assay; wild-type-like near 1 per MaveDB method text. Single scale, no unit mixing.

a5_enough_rows.note: 2,832 variants (about 2,194 missense per source paper); above the 1,500 bar for regression, but only 175 clinically labelled variants.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: <1 MB CSV plus ESM-2 embeddings for ~2,200 variants of a 335-residue region
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits; ESM embeddings on CPU in minutes.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: 2,832 rows match the 2024 paper title; 69 pathogenic / 106 benign match the reference set of 175 stated in this paper; 277+209 = 486 abnormal matches the paper's 486.

a8_label_provenance.note: Score is a physical measurement (flow-sorting of surface vs intracellular JAG1, 7 replicates). functional_consequence is a threshold of the score, so it must not be used as a feature; truth_set comes from ClinVar-style clinical classifications, independent of the assay.

B1.why: One CSV from MaveDB holds variants, scores, replicates and truth labels; verified.

B2.why: pandas read it first try, 2,832 x 17; verified.

B3.why: Single assay, single lab, single normalized score scale; verified in file.

B4.why: Scores floored at 0.0 (min exactly 0), suggesting clipping at the bottom; otherwise no censoring.

B5.why: 2,832 nucleotide rows collapse to 2,288 protein changes; synonymous/codon duplicates need averaging.

B6.why: MaveDB lists score, count columns and method text; columns are self-explanatory; verified metadata.

C1.why: Benchmark of predictors on a new trafficking assay is informative either way, but small and single-gene.

C2.why: Zero-shot predictors (AlphaMissense, ESM) and a VAMP-seq abundance predictor exist; none benchmarked on this JAG1 set.

C3.why: Weak 'unique application': membrane trafficking in a cysteine-rich secreted-pathway protein vs cytosolic abundance training data.

C4.why: MAVEs are costly lab assays, but this region is already measured almost exhaustively (97.4%).

C5.why: Source paper reports AlphaMissense/CADD enrichment; this paper gives sensitivity 87-92%, OddsPath 18.4 on 175 references.

D1.why: ESM-2 protein language model, open weights, small checkpoints on CPU.

D2.why: Cache per-variant embeddings once for ~2,200 variants; fit a ridge or small head.

D3.why: ESM-2 MIT licence; data CC0 per MaveDB record.

E1.why: Held-out position or held-out domain splits possible across 335 residues and several EGF/DSL domains.

E2.why: Domains (C2-like, DSL, EGF repeats) and residue blocks give ≥5 groups.

E3.why: Per-position mean and per-amino-acid-substitution mean are easy dummies.

E4.why: Seven replicate columns; replicate correlation 0.45-0.76 gives a noise ceiling; verified.

E5.why: Cysteine loss is a known strong cause of abnormal localization; synonymous variants should score normal.

E6.why: Label shuffle and within-domain shuffle are straightforward.

E7.why: 175 clinical truth-set variants and ClinVar give an independent clinical validation; other VAMP-seq sets in MaveDB.

E8.why: Paper's 486→610 abnormal counts reproducible from score plus their R script.

G1.why: HGVS on NM_000214.3 transcript and protein positions; mappable to UniProt P78504 and genomic coordinates.

G2.why: ProteinGym/MaveDB abundance datasets and ClinVar, joinable on gene plus protein position.

G3.why: One variant per protein change after averaging codons; clean one-to-one.

G4.why: Asks whether abundance predictors trained on cytosolic proteins transfer to secretory-pathway trafficking; modest scope.

H1.why: 2,346 normal and 486 abnormal variants, plus 106 benign and 69 pathogenic references; verified.

H2.why: One gene region, one cell line, one lab, one assay.

H3.why: Claim is precise: predicts JAG1 exon 1-7 surface localization in one cell assay.

H4.why: Paper states the assay misses NOTCH2-binding defects (4 pathogenic variants scored normal).

I1.why: Gilbert/Spinner lab (CHOP) and ClinGen variant curation groups; but they already have measurements.

I2.why: Region is ~97% measured, so a predictor changes few clinical decisions for JAG1 itself.

I3.why: Spearman on scores roughly aligned; clinical decision uses evidence-strength bins.

I4.why: Per-position means and cysteine rules may capture much of the signal.

J1.why: Real modelling: embeddings, grouped splits, transfer evaluation, noise ceiling.

J2.why: Biology is interpretable (cysteines, disulfides, domains) but needs variant-effect intuition.

J3.why: A zero-shot benchmark table alone is a shareable result in a day.

J4.why: Could be set at one week; not yet stated.

J5.why: No kill date written in NOTES.md yet.

existing_models.name: AlphaMissense (proteome-wide missense pathogenicity predictor, 2023)
existing_models.score_and_split: Precomputed scores public; source JAG1 paper (2024) reports significant enrichment of high AlphaMissense scores among 435 abnormal missense variants out of 2,194, no correlation number seen by me.

existing_models.name: Supervised VAMP-seq abundance predictor (Schulze et al., Protein Science 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: Trained on ~32,000 VAMP-seq (variant abundance by massively parallel sequencing) scores across proteins; validated on held-out experiments; exact numbers not retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Abstract notes experiment-to-experiment differences in score mapping complicate learning across datasets.

integration.partner_dataset: ProteinGym / MaveDB abundance (VAMP-seq) score sets and ClinVar
integration.join_key: Gene symbol + protein position (HGVS on NM_000214.3 / UniProt P78504)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do variant-effect models trained on cytosolic protein abundance transfer to surface trafficking of a disulfide-rich secreted-pathway protein?

controls.positive_control: Cysteine-loss variants and synonymous variants: model must rank cysteine losses as most abnormal and synonymous as normal.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle scores within domain and globally; performance must fall to per-position-mean dummy.
controls.external_validation: The 175 clinically classified variants (69 pathogenic, 106 benign) in truth_set, plus ClinVar JAG1 missense outside the reference set.

honest_claim_h3: The model predicts the surface-localization score of JAG1 exon 1-7 missense variants in one cell-based assay, and says nothing about NOTCH2-binding defects or the rest of the protein.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein language-model features of each JAG1 amino-acid change to predict whether the mutant protein still reaches the cell surface.
plain_idea.train_on: Each of about 2,200 single amino-acid changes in the first 335 residues of JAG1, described by sequence-model features; 2,832 measured variants in total (verified).
plain_idea.predict: The membrane-localization score measured by flow-sorting cells that express each variant, averaged over 7 replicates in one lab.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Tests whether general variant-effect predictors capture trafficking defects in disulfide-rich secreted proteins; even a failure tells clinical curators how far to trust predictors for such genes.

more_or_better_data.why: 2,832 variants is tiny next to ProteinGym's ~2.7M, but it covers surface trafficking of a secreted-pathway protein, a readout rare in VAMP-seq abundance training sets (~32,000 scores in Schulze 2026).

confidence_score.why: Seven replicates and per-variant std allow a noise ceiling, but one gene gives too few groups for per-region calibrated confidence.

models_beatable.why: AlphaMissense (2023) predicts pathogenicity, not this assay, so a supervised in-gene model will beat it trivially on random splits; held-out-domain is the honest test.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Other MaveDB abundance sets measure a different quantity in different assays, so adding them doesn't guarantee better prediction of JAG1 trafficking.

label_elsewhere.sources: MaveDB and ProteinGym hold many VAMP-seq abundance and surface-expression deep mutational scans (known resources); trafficking/surface readouts specifically are few.
label_elsewhere.why: Other abundance scans could serve as training data for a cross-protein model tested on JAG1, but the readouts differ.

ambitious.why: Would need a cross-protein trafficking predictor that clearly transfers to JAG1 held-out domains and improves clinical classification.

realistic.journal: Human Mutation (or Genetics in Medicine Open)
realistic.why: Publishes variant-effect predictor benchmarks on single-gene MAVEs with clinical calibration.

fallback.why: A negative transfer benchmark on one gene is still a short note.

pitch.headline: 2,832 JAG1 variants, 7 replicates each, CC0 on MaveDB, with 175 clinically classified controls in the same table.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Measures surface trafficking, not abundance, across ~97% of possible changes in a disulfide-rich region; replicate correlation 0.45-0.76 gives an explicit noise ceiling.
pitch.the_win: Show held-out-domain Spearman of a frozen ESM-2 head near the replicate ceiling, beating AlphaMissense on the 175 clinical controls.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: Quantifies how badly general predictors miss trafficking defects in secreted proteins, useful to curators weighting computational evidence.
pitch.who_wants_it: Gilbert/Spinner group (CHOP), ClinGen variant curation expert panels, and the Atlas of Variant Effects community deciding how much computational evidence to apply.

ml_idea: Benchmark zero-shot predictors (ESM-1v/ESM-2 likelihoods, AlphaMissense) and a frozen ESM-2 embedding + ridge head on JAG1 membrane-localization scores with held-out-domain splits; test transfer of a model trained on other MaveDB abundance sets.

effort.compute_note: Estimated: ~2,200 variants of a 335-residue window through ESM-2 150M on CPU at a few per second; ridge CV is seconds. Nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Compute the per-position-mean dummy under held-out-domain CV and the replicate ceiling; if AlphaMissense already reaches the ceiling, there's no room.

verdict_reason: Data is clean, open and verified (2,832 rows, CC0), but it covers one gene region that is already ~97% measured and predictors already exist, so the result is a small benchmark note with low clinical impact.
